answer: An agent registry can require a fresh proof of work for each key: a verifier checks a hash puzzle whose nonce meets a fixed difficulty before admitting bids. Each identity consumes measurable compute and electricity, so scaling a Sybil fleet raises its operating cost. A gale of cheap energy or specialized hardware can still make the barrier affordable, and the puzzle does not prove that keys belong to distinct people; jade and shale can label example agent classes without changing that limit.
